_note: Hand-researched neighborhood notes (Oct 2026). Every fact carries its source. Matched to map tracts by OSM neighborhood/park name. Sale-price figures from brokerages rest on few sales; treat as signals.

neighborhoods.name: Carlson Park

facts.text: Named for Dr. Paul Carlson Park, a 2.66-acre passive neighborhood park at Braddock Dr & Motor Ave; Culver City's first park (1927), on the site of a 1920s board-track speedway.
Redfin's neighborhood median was ~$1.01M on only 3 sales; one broker reports ~$1,650/sq ft in early 2026. Thin sample, so read it as a signal.
Culver City overall: Zillow typical value ~$1.29M (+2.0% yr); Redfin 3-month median $1.4M (+10.4%) as of Sept 2026; single-family median ~$1.6M in Q1 2026.
Served by Culver City Unified. 2025 CAASPP-based rankings put El Marino and Farragut elementaries near the top of the district, La Ballona lower.

current_projects.name: Ballona Creek Bike Path Sustainability & Accessibility Project
current_projects.detail: Solar lighting, signage and wayfinding on the creek path; construction scheduled Apr–Oct 2026, funded by Baldwin Hills Conservancy + Culver City.

current_projects.name: Ballona Creek Bike Path Extension (~2 mi to Cochran/Venice)
current_projects.detail: Design underway; ~$24.7M construction estimate; $6.4M CTC award in 2025.

current_projects.name: FY26-27 Culver City CIP
current_projects.detail: 70 capital projects; $4.65M pavement & concrete rehab; $3M street & right-of-way improvements; Bill Botts Fields renovation.

current_projects.name: Inglewood Oil Field phase-out
current_projects.detail: Culver City settlement bans new wells and ends production within city limits by 2030; County Park Needs Assessment lists converting parts of the ~1,000-acre field to parkland.

local_angles: Already has a park, so a new park adds little. The better levers are canopy (street trees on blocks with gaps) and access to the Ballona Creek path, which a cheap, well-lit connection could improve.
Culver City has its own Urban Forest Master Plan (2016) and ~15,000 city trees, so a street-tree program can go through Public Works rather than LA's StreetsLA.

neighborhoods.name: Beverlywood

facts.text: 1,354 single-family homes developed by Walter Leimert from 1940. One of LA's first tracts with binding CC&Rs; the Beverlywood Homes Association reviews size, style, color, design and landscaping.
HOA boundaries: Monte Mar Dr (N), Robertson Blvd (E), Hillcrest Country Club / Anchor Ave (W), Beverlywood St (S).
Typical home value ~$2.29M (Zillow, June 2026, +3.3% yr). Redfin monthly median $2.3M on 7 sales.
Castle Heights, just south, borders the I-10 freeway. Caltrans built a $2.1M soundwall demonstration on westbound I-10 between Motor and Military Aves in 2006.

current_projects.name: Venice Blvd Safety & Mobility Project (Palms–Mar Vista)
current_projects.detail: 4+ miles of parking-protected bike lanes, 24-hour bus lane, crosswalks and signals; completed, serves ~47,000 nearby residents.

current_projects.name: LAUSD Measure US green schoolyards
current_projects.detail: ~$1.2B for schoolyard and exterior upgrades; ~$8–12M per green-schoolyard project; priority goes to elementaries under 10% green with 275+ students.

local_angles: With values above $2M, even a 1% gain is ~$23k per home. Value-per-dollar is highest for cheap, visible amenities: canopy gaps on parkways and sidewalk/crossing quality on Robertson and toward Cheviot Hills/Rancho Park.
CC&Rs and the HOA make coordinated parkway planting easier to organize. The HOA is a natural partner.
The tract next to the I-10 (Castle Heights side) is where noise mitigation and dense roadside vegetation pay off.

regional_projects.name: Park to Playa Trail
regional_projects.detail: 13-mile trail from Baldwin Hills to the beach, completed Oct 2020 with the La Cienega pedestrian bridge. ~$23M trail plus $20.5M in amenities including the Stoneview Nature Center.

regional_projects.name: Expo (E) Line Culver City station
regional_projects.detail: Opened 2012. A before/after study found households near new stations cut driving by ~14 miles/day. No rigorous home-price study of this station was found.

regional_projects.name: MOVE Culver City (downtown bus/bike lanes)
regional_projects.detail: Inflation-adjusted sales tax on the corridor grew after 2019 while citywide stayed flat; politically contested (2023 survey: 58% strongly opposed).

regional_projects.name: LAUSD greening program
regional_projects.detail: 82 completed greening projects, 1,400+ trees planted, ~315 projects active or planned (Oct 2026); goal 30% green space systemwide.

local_costs.value: ~$300–1,250 per tree (2025-26 LA County RFP: $0.5–2M for 1,600 trees incl. maintenance); one 2022 LA Board of Public Works item implied ~$4,351 per tree including concrete cutting
$27–44M per acre all-in for recent city projects (Brooklyn Heights Park 0.19 ac $5.2M; Pio Pico 0.6 ac $26.6M incl. garage)
~$24.7M for ~2 miles (~$12M/mi) on a flood-channel right of way
